subject: Reservation hedge & fallback scenarios — dedicated capacity questionnaire
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@nebulaai.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@nebulaai.com>, procurement@nebulaai.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reservation — initial questionnaire

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking our RFP. To help our procurement and infra teams finalize a reservation, we put together a short set of clarifying questions around hedging and fallback behavior for dedicated pools:

1) Which GPU SKUs do you recommend mapping to a multi-model fleet where we run both small LLMs (<=7B) for embeddings/reranking and large chat models (~70B) for user-facing chat?
2) How do you support burst lanes beyond committed capacity (auto-burst vs queued requests)?
3) What are the tail-latency SLOs you can guarantee per reservation tier and how are canary rollouts handled?
4) How would you handle multi-region failover for US/EU workloads during regional capacity constraints?

We attached our 12-month forecast separately. Looking for concise answers today so we can slot Redwood into our shortlist.

Best,
Sophie
Infrastructure Lead — NebulaAI

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@nebulaai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation — initial questionnaire

Sophie — thanks for the clear asks. High-level answers here; attaching a sizing workbook with a worked example for the numbers you sent. Short answers below, followed by required clarifications.

1) Recommended GPU mix: H100v3 (or equivalent) for 70B chat families (we size ~80% of committed compute here), L4-class GPUs for small models and embedding workloads (cost-optimized, good for heavy concurrency), and a small pool of A100/MI250s for legacy mixed-precision jobs if you run FP16 training-type inference. We include quantized INT8 variants for most chat use-cases to save ~30–50% tokens cost with modest quality delta.

2) Burst lanes: Our Dedicated product supports two burst mechanisms — instantaneous burst (short-duration overcommit, billed at on-demand rate) and queued burst (requests enter a short queue and we pre-warm spare nodes when sustained). Policies are configurable per-route; we suggest reserving a "soft burst" buffer equal to 15–25% of your daily committed tokens for predictable traffic spikes.

3) Tail-latency SLOs: For reserved pools we target p95 < 80ms for small LLMs and p95 < 250ms for large chat models; p99 targets vary by SKU but typically p99 < 450ms for warmed H100 pools. We offer an SLA addendum for p99 if you take a higher-tier commitment. Canary rollouts: we support percentage-based canaries inside your Dedicated pool (5–20% traffic) and automatic rollback on regression signals (latency or eval score thresholds).

4) Multi-region failover: Smart routing with warm regional standby. You can choose active-active routing with regional pinning (we keep KV caches replicated when enabled) or active-passive with automated failover and throttled catch-up in the failed region. Cross-region egress/cost tradeoffs will apply — we call these out in the workbook.

Clarifying asks: can you confirm expected p99 concurrency and percent of streaming vs non-streaming requests? The workbook assumes 30% streaming for sizing worked example.

Next steps: see attached redwood_sizing_workbook.xlsx. Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through assumptions.

— Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@nebulaai.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@nebulaai.com>, procurement@nebulaai.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation — initial questionnaire

Jonas,

Thanks — attaching our traffic forecast (nebula_forecast_q1-2.csv). A few clarifications from our side:
- Target steady-state: ~100M tokens/day across US & EU, with 35% streaming chat.
- Peak: ~3x daily spikes during product launch windows (2–6 hours).
- Compliance: must be SOC2 Type II and support VPC private deployment for a subset of traffic.

Specific question: if we commit to a 12-month reserved pool with 70% usage guarantee, how many H100v3 equivalents should we hold to cover the steady-state with a 20% soft burst buffer? Also what would be the incremental cost if we exceed committed tokens by 40% during a sustained 8-hour spike?

Alex
Head of Platform — NebulaAI

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@nebulaai.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation — initial questionnaire

Alex — attaching a technical breakdown (gpu-fitment-matrix.pdf) and a conservative slotting plan. Quick answers:
- For 100M tokens/day with 35% streaming we recommend starting with a 28-node H100v3-equivalent pool (assumes model: 70B chat @ median seq 1024, 75 tok/s per H100v3 slot when quantized). That maps to ~70% of your committed capacity.
- Reserve an L4 pool sized to handle peak embedding throughput (we recommend 6–8 L4 nodes for the 65% non-stream work).
- Soft-burst buffer (20%) implies keeping an extra 6 H100v3 warm nodes or enabling queued burst. We prefer warm nodes for tail-latency-critical routes.
- Sustained 8-hour +40% overage: priced at on-demand multipliers; operationally we recommend a temporary commit uplift (pro-rated) vs repeated on-demand billing. We'll include an overage modeling tab in the workbook.

Attachment: gpu-fitment-matrix.pdf — includes per-model tokens/sec vs SKU and quantization delta.

— Karthik
Sr. Applied ML Engineer — Redwood Inference

- Overage: sustained usage beyond 120% of committed tokens billed at 1.6x on-demand; short instantaneous bursts billed at 2.2x on-demand.

We can add a DocuSign-ready quote if you confirm target commit and regions. DocuSign link will include the SLA addendum (p99 uplift) if needed.

Procurement — attaching a short runbook and SOC2 pointer in Drive. Quick notes:
- SOC2 Type II: latest report is available to customers under NDA. We'll share a redacted copy and the auditor letter via secure link; controls cover our Dedicated control plane and telemetry collection.
- Audit logs: Dedicated pools expose per-request traces and token-level billing logs to your S3 / VPC egress endpoint; retention configurable (default 90 days, enterprise add-on up to 3 years).
- Failover runbook (summary): detection -> automated circuit-breaker -> route to warm standby region -> KV cache rehydration (estimated RTO 5–12 min depending on cache size) -> throttled catch-up with burst buffer. Full details in the Drive doc.

Next steps: we've updated the sizing workbook with a dedicated tab that models the 100M tokens/day + 20% burst buffer scenario and included pricing scenarios in the quote. If you confirm target commit (suggested 70% steady-state coverage), we'll generate the DocuSign package and schedule a 30-min technical canary review.
